newsitem.title: USA: Packard Bell launches direct-sale strategy.
newsitem.headline: Packard Bell launches direct-sale strategy.

text.p: Packard Bell NEC Inc. said Wednesday it would start selling computer systems directly to small and medium-size companies, in a move the company calls a "hybrid" approach to the direct PC market.

Packard Bell's NEC Computer Systems unit unveiled a direct sales strategy, dubbed NEC NOW and scheduled for launch early in the third quarter. It will give its corporate customers a choice of buying directly from NEC or from its network of participating computer resellers and distributors.

The success of Dell Computer Corp.'s model of selling PCs directly has led many companies to look at their current way of selling PCs, from Compaq Computer Corp. to Hewlett-Packard Co. -- and now the NEC Computer Systems Division, which has been losing market share in North America.
"This will make us and our resellers more profitable," said Beny Alagem, chairman of Packard Bell NEC. "It's the logistical ability to save costs."
NEC Now will let commercial users combine the pricing advantages of direct sales with service and support from retail outlets if they want, the Sacramento, Calif.-based company said.
Initial customer orders will be fulfilled by NEC's plants in Sacramento and Fife, Wash., where NEC has build-to-order facilities for notebook computers.
Some analysts said they were sceptical of Packard Bell NEC's plans because they do not think a company can be a direct marketer of PCs at the same time it sells through distributors.

"What they are trying to do is protect their retail channel," said Louis Mazzucchelli, a Gerard Klauer Mattison analyst. "They don't want to annoy the reseller guys but they want to take advantage of being a direct supplier.
"But the corporate marketplace is getting kind of cluttered with direct suppliers. And Compaq and IBM are making noises about going to their Web site to buy PCs. ... I think it's very difficult."

The programme focuses on small and medium-size companies, the company said, adding it expected state, local and federal government agencies and educational institutions would also buy products via NEC NOW. NEC Computer Systems sells to corporate users while Packard Bell markets to the consumer. Packard Bell will continue to sell its systems through retailers.

Alagem said NEC Computer Systems has over 1,000 resellers who are all evaluating its programme, but he does not know how many will participate. Last week, Computer Reseller News, an industry trade publication, said computer resellers are expected to be upset by NEC's move.
NEC said it plans a big print advertising campaign for NEC NOW in trade publications, business magazines and daily newspapers.
The company, which Dataquest said is the world's third-largest PC supplier after Compaq and International Business Machines Corp., said it expected to double its sales force on the next few quarters.
The privately held company is 20 percent owned by Japan's NEC Corp. and 20 percent by France's Groupe Bull, with the rest held by private owners.
